testCase.description: DMN 1.6 §11.2 example table: matches("bad pattern","[0-9") -> FEEL null, B-FEEL false. DMN 1.6 §11.2 "Several FEEL built-in functions return a boolean result. In B-FEEL, those functions' semantics are modified to return false everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.4 any() example "any([false,null,true]) = true": non-null in FEEL, so unchanged in B-FEEL (§11.1).

DMN 1.6 §11.3 (derived): string length(null) is null in FEEL; B-FEEL 0 ("everywhere FEEL would return null", consistent with the spec's date(null) and string(null) examples). DMN 1.6 §11.3 "In B-FEEL, those functions' semantics are modified to return 0 everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.4 example table: lowercase(12) -> FEEL null, B-FEEL "" (the spec table writes "lowercase"; the built-in is "lower case", Table 75). DMN 1.6 §11.4 "Those methods' semantics in B-FEEL are modified to return an empty string ("") everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.4 example table: string(null) -> FEEL null, B-FEEL "". FEEL Table 73 also states string(null) = null. DMN 1.6 §11.4 "Those methods' semantics in B-FEEL are modified to return an empty string ("") everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.4 example table: day of week("a") -> FEEL null, B-FEEL "". DMN 1.6 §11.4 "Those methods' semantics in B-FEEL are modified to return an empty string ("") everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.6 example table: duration("a") -> FEEL null, B-FEEL duration("P0M"). DMN 1.6 §11.6 "return a duration of 0 months (years and months durations) or 0 seconds (days and time duration) everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.6 example table: years and months duration(null, null) -> FEEL null, B-FEEL duration("P0M"). DMN 1.6 §11.6 "return a duration of 0 months (years and months durations) or 0 seconds (days and time duration) everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.6 (derived): one invalid argument, FEEL null; B-FEEL duration("P0M") (the function returns a years and months duration). DMN 1.6 §11.6 "return a duration of 0 months (years and months durations) or 0 seconds (days and time duration) everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.6 (derived, see ambiguities): duration(null) is null in FEEL; following the spec's duration("a") example, B-FEEL duration() defaults to duration("P0M"). DMN 1.6 §11.6 "return a duration of 0 months (years and months durations) or 0 seconds (days and time duration) everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 example table: split("abc", 22) -> FEEL null, B-FEEL []. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 example table: mode([null,null,null, 1, 1,2]) -> FEEL null, B-FEEL [1]. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 (derived): the most frequent item "a" is non-numeric and is ignored, leaving mode([1, 2, 2]) = [2]; FEEL null. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 (derived): sublist() with a non-numeric start position, FEEL null; B-FEEL []. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 (derived): remove() with a non-numeric position, FEEL null; B-FEEL []. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 (derived): split(null, ",") is null in FEEL; B-FEEL []. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.7 (derived): insert before() with a non-numeric position, FEEL null; B-FEEL []. DMN 1.6 §11.7 "return an empty collection everywhere FEEL would return null for them. The mode function additionally ignores non-numeric parameters passed in their input list in B-FEEL."

DMN 1.6 §11.8 example table: range("x") -> FEEL null, B-FEEL range("(0..0)"). Asserted via equality (Table 54: ranges are equal when they have the same endpoints and inclusivity); in FEEL the left side is null and the comparison is false. DMN 1.6 §11.8 "return an empty range that does not match anything ( (0..0) ) where in FEEL it would return null."

DMN 1.6 §11.8 (derived): range(null) is null in FEEL; B-FEEL returns the empty range (0..0). DMN 1.6 §11.8 "return an empty range that does not match anything ( (0..0) ) where in FEEL it would return null."

DMN 1.6 §11.8 (derived): the default range is (0..0), whose start property (Table 68) is 0; FEEL null. DMN 1.6 §11.8 "return an empty range that does not match anything ( (0..0) ) where in FEEL it would return null."

DMN 1.6 §11.8 (derived): (0..0) has an open start, so start included (Table 68) is false; FEEL null. DMN 1.6 §11.8 "return an empty range that does not match anything ( (0..0) ) where in FEEL it would return null."

DMN 1.6 §11.8 (derived): "an empty range that does not match anything": even the endpoint 0 is not in (0..0). In FEEL range("x") is null, so this case checks the B-FEEL result only; it does not discriminate from FEEL. DMN 1.6 §11.8 "return an empty range that does not match anything ( (0..0) ) where in FEEL it would return null."

DMN 1.6 §11.3 "The C+ decision table policy being defined as the sum of the outputs yields a slightly different result in B-FEEL because the sum function semantics are altered." C+ over outputs 1, null, "x", 3: B-FEEL sum ignores the null and the string and returns 4; FEEL would return null.

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.5 sqrt(): "If number is negative it returns null" in FEEL; B-FEEL 0. DMN 1.6 §11.3 "In B-FEEL, those functions' semantics are modified to return 0 everywhere FEEL would return null for them."

DMN 1.6 §10.3.4.5 modulo(): "divisor must not be 0 (zero)", so FEEL null; B-FEEL 0. DMN 1.6 §11.3 "In B-FEEL, those functions' semantics are modified to return 0 everywhere FEEL would return null for them."
